key_insight: Evolution Strategy can train a recurrent closed-loop wall controller directly on a large turbulent channel and achieve stronger drag reduction than prior small-box gradient-based policies.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a more robust route to deployable active flow control for skin-friction reduction in turbulent channels, with better transfer to realistic domain sizes.
method: Optimize a recurrent policy with Evolution Strategy instead of gradients.
Evaluate candidate controllers on full turbulent-flow episodes using an energy-aware objective.
Train and test directly in a large channel at Re_τ ≈ 180, avoiding small-box dependence.
evidence_signal: On the large-domain channel, the ES controller reduced skin-friction drag by about 26%, compared with 17% for GRU-MARL on a minimal box and 22% for classic opposition control.
watch_item: Despite the performance gain, the controller design still needs careful validation for robustness, cost of parallel evaluations, and generalization to other Reynolds numbers or geometries.
paper_title: Gradient-free learning of a closed-loop wall controller for turbulent drag reduction
